title: Reserved-word identifiers
note: Different reserved words from the DBMIG_APP estate's "ORDER", and the column-level case is seeded three times over.

title: No primary key on a high-volume table
note: The DBMIG_APP equivalent had 2 rows. This one carries real volume, so DMS CDC genuinely cannot replicate it. PERF-002 should also fire -- the table has no indexes at all.

title: ENABLE NOVALIDATE constraint hiding orphans
note: 40 orphans rather than the single row in the DBMIG_APP estate, so the rule cannot pass by dismissing one row as noise.

title: Non-standard characters
note: Seeded with UNISTR, which is character-set independent -- U+2019, U+00E9/U+00E7 and U+20AC. The DBMIG_APP estate used CHR(146): that returns a 1-byte 0x92 value (NOT NULL), but AL32UTF8 drops the invalid byte during concatenation, so nothing was ever seeded there. See docs/04-defects.md. This one is verified present by an ASCIISTR comparison in the seed script.

title: Invalid object with stored compilation errors
note: OPS-004 (stored compilation errors in USER_ERRORS) was never exercised by the DBMIG_APP estate.

title: Unusable and invisible indexes
note: NOT PRESENT in the DBMIG_APP estate -- PERF-004 has never fired before. An unusable index stops being maintained silently; an invisible one is maintained but ignored.

title: Disabled constraint with violating data
note: NOT PRESENT in the DBMIG_APP estate -- DQ-005 has never fired before.

title: Column contains only NULLs
note: NOT PRESENT in the DBMIG_APP estate -- DQ-008 has never fired before. Requires the dataprofile probe to have real row access, so it also tests the collector's grants.

title: Byte-length character semantics
note: NOT PRESENT in the DBMIG_APP estate -- DQ-009 has never fired before. VARCHAR2(n BYTE) truncates multi-byte characters mid-character, which defect 7 makes a live hazard rather than a theoretical one.

title: Redundant index on the same leading column
object: ix_device_sub vs ix_device_sub_status, both leading on subscriber_id
note: NOT PRESENT in the DBMIG_APP estate -- PERF-008 has never fired before. Key matches on DEVICE, not on an index name: PERF-008 identifies the finding as 'DEVICE (SUBSCRIBER_ID)' -- the table plus the shared leading column -- because the redundancy is a property of the pair, not of either index alone.

title: Sensitive columns without encryption
note: national_id already existed; these names are unmistakable, so a miss here is a rule gap rather than a judgement call.
